provider: Bluesky / AT Protocol PDS — 5 MiB blob default, GC'd unless referenced

free_tier.stated: blobUploadLimit defaults to 5 * 1024 * 1024 = 5 MiB per blob, overridable per-PDS via the BLOB_UPLOAD_LIMIT env var. Per-account: bsky.app's hosted PDS is generous in practice but the protocol layer only guarantees blobs that are REFERENCED by a record.

egress.terms: Free on bsky.app's PDS and on any self-hosted PDS (it serves blobs directly from /xrpc/com.atproto.sync.getBlob). No egress meter.

tooling: XRPC: POST /xrpc/com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob (binary body + Content-Type) -> returns a `blob` ref; must then be referenced by a record (e.g. app.bsky.feed.post embed) or it is garbage-collected. Client libs: @atproto/api, atproto Python SDK, `goat` CLI.
chaining: Self-hosting a PDS removes the 5 MiB default (it is a config value), so a self-hosted PDS is bounded by YOUR disk, not Bluesky's — that makes it a hosting product, not free storage. On bsky.app's PDS the 5 MiB cap plus the reference requirement makes it useless for bulk. The usable margin is only the 'unreferenced blobs are deleted within minutes' semantics working in reverse: referenced blobs are retained indefinitely.
limits_note: per-object-cap 5 MiB default (config.ts: `blobUploadLimit: env.blobUploadLimit ?? 5 * 1024 * 1024`); blobs unreferenced within a time window (minutes) are deleted; account-level repo size limits are enforced by the AppView/PDS separately.
reliability_note: Blob GC is literal and fast — an upload without a referencing record vanishes. That is the single most important fact about this candidate.

evidence.proved: 'The blob will be deleted if it is not referenced within a time window (eg, minutes). Blob restrictions (mimetype, size, etc) are enforced when the reference is created. Requires auth, implemented by PDS.'

extras.unit_note: free_tier.unit is 'mixed' because the headline is denominated in MiB or KiB, which the schema enum does not carry; the verbatim free_tier.stated keeps the true unit.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
